authority.abi: C ABI unchanged: no exported symbol, signature, #[repr(C)] layout, allocator-seam coordinate or unsafe lint attribute changed. The DH repair adds one slot write after the authority's BN_MONT_CTX_free; the provider file is unchanged.
external_contracts: MAC_KEY is reference counted; exactly the caller holding the last reference runs ossl_mac_key_free's destructor body, and each handle owns exactly one reference.

An OSSL_PARAM array is NULL or key-terminated; an OCTET_STRING with data_size > 0 has a readable data pointer, and a UTF8_STRING is NUL-terminated. mac_key_fromdata may replace the key's priv_key/properties/cipher, releasing and NULLing each previous slot first.

MacGenCtx is exclusively owned by its gen_init caller and cleaned up exactly once. mac_gen may transfer priv_key and cipher to the new MAC_KEY; the transfer NULLs the generator's slots, and a refused ossl_prov_cipher_copy leaves the generator unchanged.

mac_export's OSSL_CALLBACK is application-controlled. No Rust &mut, non-reentrant lock or key-owned buffer is live across the call: OSSL_PARAM_BLD_to_param materialises independent copies before the callback, and the key is not touched afterwards.

A DH method's finish hook is called by DH_set_method on every transition and again by DH_free through CtxDestroy::destroy_body. dh->method_mont_p is therefore NULL or a uniquely owned live MontCtx on every entry, and the hook must clear it after release.

EC_GROUP/EC_POINT finish hooks run only from their OwnedCtx destructor bodies (ec/lib.rs:267/286 and 314/326), exactly once, immediately before the enclosing block is released; the object is never reused after the hook.
EC_KEY_METHOD.finish/keyfinish and DSO_METHOD.finish are application-owned hooks. The crate calls them at the authority's sites but cannot clear application-private state.

boundaries.mechanism: MAC_KEY refcounted ownership: ossl_mac_key_new/ossl_mac_key_free/ossl_mac_key_up_ref and CtxDestroy for MacKey
boundaries.contract: A non-NULL MAC_KEY handle owns one reference. The last ossl_mac_key_free hands the block to OwnedCtx, whose Drop runs destroy_body (secure clear of priv_key at priv_key_len, plain free of properties, cipher reset) exactly once and then releases the block; the zeroed block is a valid zero state (OB-3 obligation (b)).

boundaries.mechanism: member replacement in mac_key_fromdata: priv_key, priv_key_len, properties and cipher
boundaries.contract: Each replaced slot is adopted by OwnedBuf (secure or plain) and set to NULL before the replacement is allocated; a refused allocation leaves a valid key (NULL slot plus stale length, which every reader guards on the pointer). OSSL_PARAM data never aliases the key's own storage. The CMAC cipher replacement is ossl_prov_cipher_load's own alloc_cipher/engine transaction, which nulls replaced ownership before fetching.

boundaries.mechanism: MacGenCtx ownership and the mac_gen transfer
boundaries.contract: mac_gen_init_common returns an exclusively owned zeroed context; failure in mac_gen_init/cmac_gen_init runs mac_gen_cleanup once. mac_gen takes the cipher through ossl_prov_cipher_copy (up-ref first, failure leaves the source untouched), resets the generator's cipher, and moves priv_key to the new MAC_KEY while setting the generator's pointer to NULL and its length to 0. mac_gen_cleanup may therefore run on either the pre-transfer or post-transfer state.

key_to_params completes and OSSL_PARAM_BLD_to_param copies every value into a builder-owned block before param_cb is invoked. mac_export holds only its own tmpl/params locals across the callback, forms no reference to MacKey after the call, and frees params/tmpl regardless of the callback's answer. A callback that frees the key cannot invalidate the exported parameter block; a callback that retains the pointer past return violates the OSSL_CALLBACK contract.

boundaries.mechanism: DH method finish hook and the cached Montgomery context
boundaries.contract: DH_set_method runs the outgoing table's finish and then init; DH_free runs finish once through CtxDestroy::destroy_body. On every entry dh->method_mont_p is NULL or the object's uniquely owned live context. dh_finish releases it through BN_MONT_CTX_free and writes NULL back, so a second transition/free is a no-op and the next key operation rebuilds through BN_MONT_CTX_set_locked rather than taking its non-NULL fast path with freed storage.

defects.class: freed-but-not-cleared cached pointer (M17-D1/M20-D2 class): double free and use-after-free across a method transition
defects.description: dh_finish called BN_MONT_CTX_free(dh->method_mont_p) without clearing the slot. DH_set_method invokes the outgoing method's finish on every transition (dh/object.rs:143), and DH_free invokes it again through the destructor body (dh/object.rs:339). A second finish therefore released the same MontCtx twice, and a key operation after the transition found the freed pointer through BN_MONT_CTX_set_locked's non-NULL fast path (bn/mont.rs:309-312).
defects.fix: Clear dh->method_mont_p immediately after BN_MONT_CTX_free, with the divergence and §17 rationale at the hook. Regression control `dh::key::tests::the_finish_hook_clears_the_mont_cache_it_releases` asserts the slot is NULL after DH_set_method and then exercises the second finish through DH_free. The same control was observed to fail with the clear temporarily removed.

residuals.disposition: RETAINED - authority-faithful, documented at the site
residuals.description: mac_gen_set_params overwrites gctx->priv_key without releasing the previous secure block (authority mac_legacy_kmgmt.c:425 does the same). A caller that sets a private key twice on one generator context leaks the first block, including secret contents. The crate sets the slot to NULL before the replacement allocation, so cleanup cannot release the stale pointer; this is a resource/secret-hygiene leak, not UB, and is preserved for authority behaviour. Authority differential is NOT_RUN.

The EC group/point finish hooks free their owned field elements without NULLing them. They are reached only from the owning EcGroup/EcPoint OwnedCtx destructor, exactly once, immediately before the enclosing block is released; no path re-enters them or reuses the object. This is documented rather than changed to avoid altering authority teardown order.

EC_KEY_METHOD.finish/keyfinish and DSO_METHOD.finish are application-owned callbacks. The crate calls them at the authority's sites (including method transitions for EC_KEY) but cannot know or clear application-private cached state; a hook must tolerate the authority's call sequence. All built-in EC tables set these slots to None, and the DSO refcount tests pin the crate's own reentrancy behaviour.
